comparisons.peer_topic: USPB Financial Metrics and Branch Presence
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024, USPB had 642 retail bank branches in six key metropolitan areas, $171 billion in outstanding credit card balances, $89 billion in deposits, $46 billion in mortgages, and $5 billion in personal and small business loans.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and C disclose significant balances in credit card loans as a primary component of their consumer or retail lending portfolios. BAC reports that its average total loans grew to $309.5 billion, with credit card loans cited as a key driver of this growth alongside small business and vehicle loans. Similarly, C's USPB segment reports holding $171 billion in outstanding credit card balances, representing the largest loan category within that specific segment compared to its $46 billion in mortgages and $5 billion in other loans. While BAC focuses on the aggregate growth of its Consumer Banking average loans, C details the static year-end composition of its USPB loan book, highlighting the materiality of credit cards in both institutions' consumer-facing operations.

comparisons.peer_summary: Provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024 from $1.14 billion in 2023, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio.
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address the credit quality and performance metrics of credit card portfolios. BAC attributes the growth in its Consumer Lending average loans ($309.5 billion) to increases in credit card balances, implying active lending growth. In contrast, GS focuses on the cost of holding these loans, reporting that its provision for credit losses increased to $1.54 billion in 2024, primarily driven by net charge-offs in the credit card portfolio. While BAC highlights the volume expansion of credit cards, GS highlights the deterioration or cost associated with the credit card portfolio's performance through increased provisions.
